claim.quote: We find that the state of matter created at RHIC cannot be described in terms of ordinary color neutral hadrons.

key_value_text.quote: We find that the state of matter created at RHIC cannot be described in terms of ordinary color neutral hadrons.
key_value_text.value: The matter formed in central Au+Au collisions at RHIC behaves as a strongly-interacting, opaque, rapidly-thermalizing system inconsistent with a picture of ordinary color-neutral hadrons.

name: Formation of Dense Partonic Matter in Relativistic Nucleus-Nucleus Collisions at RHIC: Experimental Evaluation by the PHENIX Collaboration
notes: Historically significant PHENIX 'white paper' from RHIC's widely publicised 2005 announcements. Per the wave-3 brief, recorded with the collaboration's own title wording and result_type 'measurement' (never 'discovery').

significance.locator: arXiv:nucl-ex/0410003, abstract (no single significance/sigma value stated)
significance.note: A collaboration-wide assessment paper, not a single-significance result. Recorded as a measurement, never as a discovery or observation, per the brief's explicit instruction ('never discovery').

summary.plain: In 2005, the PHENIX collaboration published its own detailed review of RHIC gold-ion collision data, concluding the hot matter formed behaves nothing like an ordinary gas of colourless particles -- consistent with a strongly interacting quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: PHENIX's 2005 white paper (Nucl. Phys. A 757, 184-283) evaluates RHIC Au+Au data and concludes the created matter cannot be described in terms of ordinary color-neutral hadrons, supporting a picture of dense, strongly-interacting partonic matter.

title: Formation of Dense Partonic Matter in Relativistic Nucleus-Nucleus Collisions at RHIC: Experimental Evaluation by the PHENIX Collaboration
why_it_matters: One of the four RHIC collaborations' widely reported 2005 assessments that reframed RHIC collisions as producing a strongly-coupled, nearly-perfect liquid of quarks and gluons.
